new_written_arguments: CRT differential projectors preserve ORIGINAL forms because they are polynomials in P; each nonzero exponential-polynomial component would lie both in a point submodule and V^>-1, contradicting strictness.

Every nonzero original tame period has a nonrational ordinary moment resolvent. A normalized eventually pure original volume period is nonzero polynomial, so no nonconstant eventually pure phase is tame in the stated senses.

For arbitrary eventually pure phases, the original unit lies outside V_0^>-1, and outside V_0^>-N-1 when the unit period has degree N. This is a necessary origin defect, not sufficient for purity or failure.

A proper P1xP1 completion of uv+z^2=1 verifies tameness of z-1 directly. Its original unit period is (1-e^-2t)/(2t), while a t-dependent amplitude has period 1 and gives an actual nonsplit polynomial-period submodule.
not_claimed: Wildness sufficient for purity or failure
